text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Capital from young Russian businesspeople helped Boris Yeltsin win presidential elections in 1996, says Boris Berezovsky, the prominent businessman and politician.

- Ruling authorities and the opposition demonstrated unprecedented unity in deciding the future of the Far East's Primorye regional Governor Yevgeny Nazdratenko, calling for early elections to settle the region's economic crisis.
- The government is preparing pension reform which is said to include cutting social benefits and raising the pension age to 70 years from 55 for women and 60 for men.
- The State Duma lower house of Russian parliament postponed until autumn passing a law that would introduce state control over personal spending.
- The State Duma's budget committee turned down the new tax code prepared by the government.
SEVODNYA

- The killing of Larisa Nechayeva, the director general of Russia's top soccer club, Spartak Moscow, shocked the country's soccer community with the mafia's first open demonstration of force in the sports world.
- Russia is to receive a $600 million World Bank loan for restructuring its economy.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is to chair a special committee on fighting illegal currency export.
- Despite new regulations chanelling federal budget operations to the state treasury, commercial banks are still likely to have access to budget funds.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- It has been almost a year since Boris Yeltsin was reelected president. But the political situation and the president's entourage resemble that of 1992.
- The government's perspectives on economic reform are largely based on unrealistic statistics, economic experts say.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- The state should control tariffs, but the tariff system should be flexible, says Railway Minister Nikolai Aksenenko.
SOVIETSKAYA ROSSIA
- Bankruptcy of the new reformers' economic course is obvious, says Gennady Zyuganov, the Communist leader.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
